items.title: Medicare Advantage insurer accused of upcoding by a whistleblower settles False Claims Act lawsuit for $22.5M - HealthExec
items.reason: This is a direct enforcement action—a False Claims Act settlement involving a Medicare Advantage payer for upcoding violations, which is a core payer litigation and regulatory enforcement topic.
items.summary: A Medicare Advantage insurer settled a False Claims Act whistleblower lawsuit for $22.5 million over allegations of upcoding. The settlement resolves claims that the payer systematically inflated diagnosis codes to increase reimbursement from CMS, a practice that impacts both government oversight and provider relationships within the MA network. This enforcement action directly affects revenue-cycle operations for providers contracted with the settling insurer and signals heightened CMS scrutiny of coding practices across the MA industry.

items.title: Elevance Health sued again over out-of-network penalty - Modern Healthcare
items.reason: This item directly reports litigation against Elevance Health (formerly Anthem) regarding out-of-network facility penalties, which is explicitly cited in the topic definition as a core payer enforcement concern.
items.summary: Elevance Health faces another lawsuit over its out-of-network penalty practices. The litigation targets the payer's policy of penalizing providers for using out-of-network facilities, a practice that has drawn repeated legal challenges. This type of claim-denial and provider-penalty enforcement action is directly relevant to revenue-cycle teams managing Elevance contracts and reimbursement disputes, as it may influence payer policy adjustments and member/provider dispute resolution going forward.
